title: Report a fault to support
intro: Report a fault to support so that they can help you without a lot of follow-up questions.
transfer: In your next fault report to IT, write five things: the steps, the exact message, what you expected, what you already tried, device and browser.

content.goal: At the end support knows what you did, which message appeared, what you expected, what you already tried and which device and browser you use.
content.aiRole: You play Marco from the internal IT support for the fictional program “Planwerk”. The person in the chat reports a fault to you. You can only help once you know: which steps led to the fault, the exact wording of the error message (with code), what should actually have happened, what has already been tried and which device and browser they are using. You cannot see the person's material. Ask kindly about whatever is still missing: only one question at a time, at most 2 to 3 short sentences. If a detail is vague (“it doesn't work”, “some error”), ask specifically. Do not guess and do not offer a solution while details are missing. Once everything is there, say thank you, sum up the report in one sentence and say that you will look into the fault now.
content.opening: Hello, this is Marco from Planwerk support. What happened?

material.title: What happened to you (made up)
lines: You wanted to export the monthly report as a PDF.
You have already reloaded the page.
You use Firefox on your laptop.

criteria.label: What you did
criteria.hint: Which steps did you take before the fault appeared?

criteria.label: Exact error message
criteria.hint: What exactly does the message say, with the code?

criteria.label: What you already tried
criteria.hint: What have you already tried to fix the fault?

criteria.label: Device and browser
criteria.hint: Which device and which browser do you use?

fallbackReplies: Thanks for the report. What exactly did you do, step by step, before the fault appeared?
I see. Which message appears exactly? Ideally word for word, with the code.
And what should actually have happened?
What have you already tried, and on which device and in which browser does it happen?
Thanks, with that I can reproduce the fault and look into it. You can finish the lesson now.

title: Describe a problem so others can help
intro: A short explainer video with two questions along the way.
transfer: With the next error message, copy the text word for word before you close the window, and send it to IT with your device and browser.

scenes.caption: “It doesn't work” hardly helps support. Whoever is meant to help has to be able to reproduce the fault.
Describe the steps up to the fault. And say what should actually have happened.
Copy the error message word for word, with the code. Support finds “PW-412” at once, “some error” not.
Finally: what have you already tried? And which device and browser do you use?

questions.prompt: What is the best way to pass on an error message?
options: Explained briefly in your own words
Copied word for word with the code
questions.explanation: The exact text with the code shows support at once which fault it is. Your own words lose details.

questions.prompt: What is missing here? “I wanted to save the report as a PDF. After Export → PDF, error PW-412 appeared. Reloading didn't help.”
options: The exact wording of the error message
The device and the browser you use
What you have already tried out
questions.explanation: Goal, steps, message and attempt are there. Without device and browser, support can hardly reproduce the fault.

title: Find the right tool
intro: Work out with the AI what a tool must do for your team's task before you choose one.
transfer: Before the next tool choice, write down three lines: what it must do, who uses it and with which data.

content.goal: At the end you have a short list of requirements: what the tool must do, who uses it, with which data and on which devices.
content.aiRole: You are a learning coach. The learner is to choose a tool for a shared task list for their team (see material). Help them clarify the requirements first: what must the tool do? Who uses it, including people outside the company? Which data goes into it, and may that data leave the company? On which devices and with which programs do people work? Never name a product or brand and do not recommend a particular tool, even if the learner asks for one: in that case, steer kindly back to the requirements. Ask questions instead of giving solutions: only one question at a time, at most 2 to 3 short sentences. After three to four answers, ask the learner to sum up their requirements in a short list.
content.opening: Before we talk about tools: what exactly should the task list do for your team?

material.title: The task (made up)
lines: You need a shared task list for a project.
Two external partner companies are to work on it too.
Some people often work on the go, on their phones.
The tasks also contain customer names.

criteria.label: Clarify the requirements
criteria.hint: What must the tool do, for whom, and with which data?

criteria.label: Devices and programs
criteria.hint: On which devices and with which programs does the team work?

fallbackReplies: Good. Who all works with this list, and does anyone from outside need access?
Which data goes into the tasks? Is there anything that must not leave the company?
And where do people work: on a laptop in the office, on a phone on the go, or both?
Now sum up your requirements in a short list: what must the tool absolutely be able to do?
Thanks. With this list you can compare tools before you decide. You can finish the lesson now.
